The team played its home games in [[Lexington, Kentucky]] for the 40th consecutive season at [[Rupp Arena]], with a capacity of 23,500. The team was led by [[John Calipari]], in his seventh season. They were a member of the [[Southeastern Conference]]. They finished the season 27–9, 13–5 in SEC play to win a share of the SEC regular season championship. They defeated [[2015–16 Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball team|Alabama]], [[2015–16 Georgia Bulldogs basketball team|Georgia]], and [[2015–16 Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball team|Texas A&M]] to be champions of the [[2016 SEC men's basketball tournament|SEC tournament]]. space.JPG|thumb|Recruit [[Isaiah Briscoe]] at the [[2015 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]]]] [[Isaiah Briscoe]], originally from [[Newark, New Jersey]], was the third highest rated point guard that Calipari had signed at Kentucky. He committed to Kentucky on November 13, live on [[ESPNU]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/11871615/skal-labissiere-isaiah-briscoe-commit-kentucky-wildcats|title=Kentucky gains 2015's top class|access-date=2015-04-06|date=2014-11-13|publisher=[[ESPN.com]]}} He chose Kentucky over [[St. John's Red Storm men's basketball|St. John's]]. He helped lead Team USA at the 2014 FIBA Americans U18 Championships to a gold medal.{{cite web|url=http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/111414aaa.html|title=Kentucky Adds Three for 2015|access-date=2015-04-06|date=2014-11-14|publisher=University of Kentucky|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150412181802/http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/111414aaa.html|archive-date=2015-04-12|url-status=dead}} He was a McDonald's All-America and [[Jordan Brand Classic]] game selection.{{cite news|url=http://www.kentucky.com/2015/01/28/3665975/uk-signee-briscoe-named-mcdonalds.html|title=UK signees Briscoe, Murray named McDonald's All-Americans|access-date=2015-04-06|date=2015-01-28|newspaper=[[Lexington Herald-Leader]]}}{{cite news|url=http://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/recruiting/2015/03/05/jordan-games-uk-signees/24428427/|title=Four UK signees chosen to Jordan Brand Classic|access-date=2015-04-06|date=2015-03-05|newspaper=[[The Courier-Journal]]}} [[Skal Labissière]], originally from [[Haiti]], was a consensus top five player in the 2015 class. He moved to [[Memphis, Tennessee]] from his home country after an earthquake disaster in January 2010.{{cite web|url=https://www.sbnation.com/college-basketball/2014/10/27/7081065/skal-labissiere-recruiting-memphis-kentucky|title=Top recruit Skal Labissiere says he's playing for a prep school that might not exist|access-date=2015-04-06|date=2014-10-27|publisher=SB Nation}} Labissière and Briscoe committed on the same night, minutes apart, on ESPNU. Labissière chose Kentucky over [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]]. Calipari has likened Labissière to former Wildcats [[Anthony Davis]] and [[Nerlens Noel]]. [[Charles Matthews (basketball)|Charles Matthews]], originally from [[Chicago|Chicago, Illinois]], was the first commitment in the 2015 signing class on February 26, 2014.{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/chicago/story/_/id/10520316/charles-matthews-chicago-st-rita-commits-kentucky-wildcats|title=Charles Matthews commits to UK|access-date=2015-04-06|date=2014-02-26|newspaper=[[The Courier-Journal]]}} Once considered a top-15 player in class, Matthews finished in the top-60 recruits on the four recruiting services. [[Mychal Mulder]], originally from [[Windsor, Ontario]], was the first signee after the conclusion of the 2015 season. Mulder helped lead [[Vincennes University]] to a 33–2 record, earned JUCO All-America honors and was rated the 13th-best junior-college prospect in the country by 247Sports.com's composite ranking. He chose Kentucky over [[Creighton Bluejays men's basketball|Creighton]], [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]], and [[Wichita State Shockers men's basketball|Wichita State]] at a press conference on April 28.{{cite news|url=http://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/kentucky/2015/04/28/four-star-juco-guard-mulder-picks-kentucky/26526735/|title=Four-star JUCO guard Mulder picks Kentucky|access-date=2015-04-28|date=2015-04-29|newspaper=[[Courier-Journal]]|author=Tucker, Kyle}}{{cite news|url=http://www.indystar.com/story/sports/college/indiana/2015/04/28/mychal-mulder-juco-kentucky-indiana-vincennes/26505009/|title=Vincennes guard also considered Wichita State and Creighton|access-date=2015-04-29|date=2015-04-29|newspaper=[[Lexington Herald-Leader]]|author=Roberts, Ben}} [[Jamal Murray]], originally from [[Kitchener, Ontario]], was the last signee for the 2016 season. Murray's stock began to soar following a breakout performance at the [[Nike Hoop Summit]] against the USA Basketball Team. ''USA Today'' announced its initial coaches poll on October 15 with Kentucky ranked as No. 1 in the country, which was also shared with [[2015–16 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|North Carolina]].{{cite news |url=http://sportspolls.usatoday.com/ncaa/basketball-men/polls/coaches-poll/2015/1/|title=Top 25 Teams, Week 1 |work=USA Today |date=October 15, 2015}} The [[Associated Press]] announced on October 31 that Kentucky was ranked No. 2 to start the season in its initial poll of the season.{{cite web |url=http://collegebasketball.ap.org/poll/2016/1 |title=The AP Top 25 Poll |work=[[Associated Press|AP]] |date=November 2, 2015 |access-date=2015-11-19 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151117233043/http://collegebasketball.ap.org/poll/2016/1 |archive-date=2015-11-17 |url-status=dead }} ===Events=== On May 21 Kentucky released the non-conference portion of its schedule.{{cite web|url=http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/052115aaa.html|title=Wildcats Unveil Formidable Non-Conference 2015-16 Schedule|access-date=2015-05-21|date=2015-05-21|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|work=UKAthletics|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150524055644/http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/052115aaa.html|archive-date=2015-05-24|url-status=dead}} The schedule is highlighted by marquee match-ups at Rupp Arena and across the country. Kentucky will travel to Chicago to play defending National Champion Duke in the annual [[Champions Classic]], to Los Angeles to play UCLA for its first ever game at [[Pauley Pavilion]], to Miami to play South Florida and former assistant [[Orlando Antigua]], and to Brooklyn to play against Ohio State in the annual [[CBS Sports Classic]]. Kentucky will also host Arizona State and in-state rival Louisville. It included player introductions, a speech by Calipari, and a scrimmage.{{cite web|url=http://www.ukathletics.com/news/top-six-moments-from-big-blue-madness-2015-10-16-2015|title=Top six moments from Big Blue Madness 2014|access-date=2014-10-16|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|work=UKathletics.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151020011613/http://www.ukathletics.com/news/top-six-moments-from-big-blue-madness-2015-10-16-2015|archive-date=2015-10-20|url-status=dead}} The Blue-White scrimmage was the first live game for the team.
